title.narrative: Life-saving food security and livelihood support and WASH services to vulnerable people with extreme severity in Pigi/Canal.

description.narrative: Cordaid/ADA will target the most vulnerable, food insecure, households. For beneficiary targeting the cluster standards will be used. Criteria for beneficiary selection include: • HHs with children under 5 • Women headed households. • Child headed households. • Elderly headed households and persons with specific needs (PSN) such as HH with chronically ill, PWD, PLW. • Type of shelter and condition the beneficiaries are being accommodated in now. • Households with no basic items /or those who have lost most of their properties during displacement. • Households with SAM/MAM cases.

Jonglei is one of the states severely affected by the rains and consequent floods, and one of its most affected counties is Pigi/Canal. In Pigi/Canal the floods reached the highest point in September 2021, since than displacing over 78.00 people. 53.000 people out of these are now facing IPC4+ when the lean season has not even started. Pigi/Canal has an estimated population of 106,424 people: 73% of the population has been affected/displaced by the floods and 50% of these are in IPC4/5 classification (FSNMS+, Feb ’22). The number of vulnerable people is likely to increase as it still has to be seen of people will be able to use the next planting season (starting from March/April). The increased food insecurity is a result of the large displacements (many people have not been able to return to their villages), destructions of livelihoods and homes, missing or dead animals and submersion of farmlands and subsequent destruction of crops, due to the floods. At the same time, people have reduced access to basic services and water infrastructures are unsafe for drinking. The rapid assessment done by Reach (‘Jan 22) confirms this information: the flooding in 2020/2021 coincide with the harvest period, therefor in both years very few households were able to harvest. Due to the flooding and diseases, many people list their cattle, and only few households still own livestock, if they are due, it has been moved further away, while the population typically relies on livestock during the lean season. People are relying on HFA (Hum Food Assistance), wild foods and fishing, but ratios for HFA have reduce, are shared with more than one household and floods have challenges to access the HFA distributions. Continued reliance on wild foods is likely to result in sickness for children as well as the elderly. Supplies in markets have also reduced due to the flooding’s. Identified needs by the community are increased HFA, medicines, shelter items, canoes, fishing nets and flashlights. This data confirms the FSNMS+ report, where the projection is that food insecurity in Pigi will increase further, with even IPC5 levels. In Pigi/Canal, a limited number of actors is present, Cordaid has a long-term history in Pigi, although currently no ongoing projects; our local partner ADA also recently started in Pigi and has presence on the ground. Limited efforts to address the current gaps are ongoing, and the needs are huge.
In summary people are in urgent need of humanitarian assistance for their survival, as food insecurity is projected to increase even further over the next few months. At the same time, access to basic services has reduced drastically and there is need for save drinking water. As community structures are changing as well, due to reduction of traditional coping mechanisms, it will as well be important to engage with the communities to look beyond the next three months.
To provide life-saving assistance to 6,000 severely food insecure people in Pigi/Canal through an FSL and WASH intervention.

title.narrative: Humanitarian, DRA key result indicators
WSH-R4: Number of people having access to sufficient and safe water for domestic use

description.narrative: Access: maximum distance to water point 500m, queuing time less than 15min, filling time maximum 3 min/20 litres or as locally agreed. Water access should be during the whole period of implementation unless action is mostly related to building the local water delivery capacity. Sufficient: covering basic needs, i.e. 7.5-15 l/p/d or as locally agreed. Safe: 1) low risk of faecal contamination, 2) No faecal coliforms detectable in any 100-ml sample, 3) For piped water supplies, or for all water supplies at times of risk or presence of diarrhoea epidemic, water is treated with a disinfectant to achieve free chlorine residual at the tap of 0.5 mg per litre and turbidity is below 5 NTU, 4) If for a short period, water which is contaminated chemically or radiologically is used, no (significant probability of) negative health effect is (likely to be) detected. Domestic use: drinking, cooking and personal hygiene (incl. laundry)

title.narrative: FSC-R2: Number of people enabled to meet their basic food needs (non-cash)

description.narrative: Basic food needs: assistance, combined with beneficiaries' own resources, to international standard of 2100 kcal per person per day for the period of the action. Any kind of transfer modality (in-kind, voucher, cash) and combination thereof with objective to ensure immediate access to the necessary food commodities. This may include supplementary foods provided alongside general distribution for vulnerable people.

title.narrative: FSC-R1: Number of people provided with resources to protect and start rebuilding livelihoods assets

description.narrative: Resources that enable people to protect and rebuild their livelihood assets include seeds, livestock, tools, business grant, etc. Any kind of transfer modality (in-kind, voucher, restricted cash) and combination thereof to support, protect and enable the restoration/protection/access of/to livelihood assets.

title.narrative: WSH-R6: Number of people reached with hygiene promotion/awareness raising activities

description.narrative: Hygiene promotion/awareness raising activities. Could be training, campaigns, radio broadcasts, flyers etc. Excludes the distribution of Hygiene/dignity kits that should be covered under WHS-I1.

title.narrative: WSH-R1: Number of people having regular access to soap to meet hygienic needs

description.narrative: Regular and timely access: 250g soap/p/m for personal hygiene, 200g soap/p/month for laundry. This includes hygiene/dignity kits. Access may be in-kind or though voucher distribution or through unconditional restricted cash to enable beneficiary to buy soap (without compromising access to other basic needs). Distributed items need to be culturally acceptable i.e. take into account local practice and expectations.

title.narrative: The Humanitarian Response was Timely

description.narrative:
SPHERE: Communities and people affected by crisis, including the most vulnerable groups, consider that the timing of the assistance and protection they receive is adequate. DRA: timely depends on the nature of the acute crisis (slow versus sudden onset). If it is an acute sudden onset crisis a response is considered timely if we decide to respond within 48 hours and if we initiate the response within 72 hours. If it is a slow onset crisis, it is timely if we initiate the response in 3 weeks after we decide that the crisis meets the criteria of an acute crisis.
The applicable definition depends on the type of crisis (protracted versus acute). The SPHERE definition should be used in more protracted crisis where there is (more) time to conduct assessments and measure satisfaction of the response in the eyes of people affected. The DRA definition should be used for acute crises, where it is more important to initiate the response as soon as possible and look at our own processes.
